title: get_mcp_readiness_attestation is NOT broken -- resolved, full correction chain recorded
summary: get_mcp_readiness_attestation's 'Token lookup failed' error was first attributed to a Supabase-level query error in requireAssistantToken.ts, ruling out wrong project/schema/table/column/RLS. That conclusion was superseded after a genuine restart revealed the local mcp-api backend service simply was not running (ps aux / pm2 list empty). Starting it and running npm run mcp:attest produced a clean passing attestation. Supersede any stale intelligence claiming readiness attestation is broken.
retrievalQuestions: Is get_mcp_readiness_attestation currently broken, and what was the actual root cause of its Token lookup failed error?
Why did requireAssistantToken.ts appear to fail even though its Supabase query logic was correct?
How do you fix a Token lookup failed error from the MCP readiness attestation tool?

futureAgentInstructions.whenThisAppears: A future agent sees get_mcp_readiness_attestation fail or finds stale intelligence claiming it is a known-broken tool
doNot: Leave or propagate stale intelligence stating readiness attestation is broken -- this finding supersedes it
Diagnose a Supabase/schema-level defect in requireAssistantToken.ts before confirming the local mcp-api service process is actually running
proveBeforeClaiming: ps aux or pm2 list shows the mcp-api service running before claiming the attestation tool is healthy or broken
npm run mcp:attest produces a fresh, passing runtime/mcp-readiness-attestation/latest.json
